verses.verse:
सौम्याकृतिः, प्रलम्बासुः समदृष्टिः, सुनादकृत्।
नातिवक्र, शिरः कायो, मन्द्रतार नियन्त्रितः।६८।
verses.text: Calm in appearance, long-breathed, with a steady gaze, making a good sound; with head and body not too bent; controlled in the low and high registers;

verses.verse:
सीतकार रहितः, सूक्ष्मों, मुखरन्ध्र वशीकृतः।
सुकम्पितश्च फूप्कारो ज्ञेयो दशगुणान्वितः।६९।
verses.text: free of hissing, fine, held under control at the mukharandhra (mouth-hole), and well vibrated: blowing should be known to have these ten qualities.

commentary.text: The breath for the flute has the ten qualities above, and opposite to them there can be as many faults. The practitioner has to avoid the faults and move towards the qualities; those qualities are explained here. — (1) While blowing, the face should be pleasant and calm. (2) The breath should come out for a long time. (3) The gaze should be steady and the eyes open naturally. (4) There should be sweetness in the breath. (5) The body should not be too bent. (6) The breath should be so controlled that the notes of the mandra (low), madhya (middle) and tāra (high) saptaka (octave) can be produced at will. (7) The face should not be distorted while blowing. (8) No kind of hissing should be heard with the breath, or before or after it. (9) The stream of the breath should be so thin that it can produce sound even in small holes. (10) There should be a regular vibration in the breath that is heard like a wave. — All these qualities are for the āḍī (transverse) and the Tripurā flute.

For the flute with a jībh (fipple) the following points should be kept in mind. (1) Do not take the flute far into the mouth; as far as possible, keep it at the front edge of the lips. (2) Tighten the breath in proportion to the room there is in the jibbhī (fipple) built inside the flute, so that there is control over the sounds of two octaves. (3) Saliva should not come along with the breath. — The above qualities and faults should be watched closely in the early period. Some people even make use of a mirror.

If one listens carefully to the sound of one's own breath, an irregular vibration will be seen in the sound, like the flickering flame of a lamp. Taking that as a fault, several actions for regular vibration are described in the following śloka.
